div.div:
Product discovery
is completely in the problem space. We need to know what users we want to serve and what problems they have. We want to find what user problems would be most impactful to solve. When starting out on a new product, it's quite useful to look for a niche market to serve. Normally there will be niche markets that are underserved by larger competitors and it's an easy way to gain some market share and get customers fast.
For large/new initiatives this step could be a large effort. For existing products this will normally be a smaller list mostly harnessing what we learn from current customers to serve them better.
When a new problem is large enough and different enough than previous problems, we need to develop a PRD. We need to clarify who this problem and why we should solve this problem, how it make sense within our product, how impactful solving this problem is, estimated user base and feature impacts.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 418px; height: 1px; padding-top: 7px; margin-left: 500px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Solutioning
Across disciplines, we work to determine the solution to our user's problem turning a PRD into an Epic complete with high level designs and architecture documentation. The solutioning phase can happen whenever we have a new PRD ready to dig into. This will provide us with healthy backlog of Epics. We will better understand our users the more Epics we have. We will also have better planning and road mapping sessions due to this better understanding. The healthy backlog will allow us to pick higher impact work at the right time.
Design looks over the PRD created by product and starts to develop how this feature fits into our products and creates a high-level design to solve the user's problem. This design will be attached to the Epic. Engineering will use the PRD as input into architecture decisions that need to be made to solve the user's problem. When necessary, engineering will draft a proposal solution to the problem along with a ballpark level of effort estimate. This information will be attached to the Epic.
Design and Engineering work together to hash out the solution. Having this collaboration early, allows engineers to better understand how a user interacts with the product and designers to better understand technological limitations. Ultimately this will lead to more efficiencies in the process.
While the Design and Engineering Teams are working on solutioning, Product is there to answer all questions and refine the PRD as needed. Product also will validate the proposed solution to make sure the solution will in fact solve the user's problem. Once in agreement, product will create the epic, linking all relevant documentation.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 358px; height: 1px; padding-top: 25px; margin-left: 1030px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Planning
We've been creating a lot of Epics and PRDs and really learning our users. Now we look over these potential features and pick the ones that have the most impact for the least amount of effort and slot those first into the roadmap. We can plan ahead with the knowledge we have. As we continue making Epics, we will update the roadmap to reflect and prioritize changes based on our user's needs. Also, there will be some allotted capacity given to engineering for working on Tech Debt and security needs.
Now that we know which epics we will want to work on soon. Design will take their high level design and begin more detail to them. And, as design evolve, they may need to make update to the original proposed design to maintain consistency.
Now that we know which Epics we will work on next, we need to look at our ADR and flesh out any missing details due to any design updates or and to account for any evolution of our Architecture since the original ADR was proposed.
Product does the detailed design and creates user stories to solve the users problem and states the design requirements. Product will work with engineering to refine the tickets as needed to make the stories actionable and clear for efficient development.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 278px; height: 1px; padding-top: 185px; margin-left: 1457px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Delivering
We now have our quarters planned and we roughly have our sprints planned. Engineering will now execute the solutions through the user stories. Also, some engineering capacity is utilized to resolve tech debt, security needs, and any bugs that come up that product have deemed a priority to resolve.
After software is developer and tested by engineering, product will perform reviews to queue up features for weekly customer releases. Engineering will provide assistant with deploying queued up features.

div.div:
Req Gathering
1. current customer feedback - gets feedback from current customers through an idea/help customer portal we provide to customers, email comms, meetings, etc
2. user research - product - UX - has meetings for user research documents outcome and added ideas to idea portal
3. user testing - product - UX - user testing sessions, clickable prototypes, A/B UI testing to help clarify problem space and solution space
4. Sales - meets with potential customers and put in the idea portal any product ideas for consideration
5. partnerships - meetings can generate some integration ideas for overlapping customer bases, can also form large new ideas and will put these ideas into our idea portal suggested tool for idea portal https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/product-discovery

div.div:
Getting to a PRD
product - (PO and UQ) - goes over any new inputs to turn these requirements into personas and product requirements docs. Has meetings with the folks who generated the inputs as needed.
Decision Point -
Put idea on hold - we determine our current customer base won't benefit enough from solving this problem Move idea into user research activity to better flesh it out, problem space or impact isn't clear enough Move to POC activity - problem is well defined but the solution is unclear and we decide to do user testing, get clickable prototypes in front of user, engineering to build POC is needed to validate assumptions. Idea to get user feedback early to better inform solutioning/product as needed Move forward to PRD as usual

div.div:
POC before PRD
The POC process can be triggered by user testing activities and product/engineering deciding an idea is worthy of building and testing a POC. POC can be a user activity such as providing clickable mockups. POC can also involve engineering effort to build a POC and provide this to the customer. When building a POC, there will be a meeting to go over POC documentation which will be a bit like a lightweight PRD mixed with some successful criteria that will determine if we should move forward with a user solution to this problem or not. We might want to timebox an engineering POC's development time and fail the POC if we cannot meet the deadline. This limits that the solution may have ended up being too complex or not possible. Other fail criteria could surround if the user feedback of the POC was positive enough.

div.div:
Solutioning
When product finalizes a PRD, they provide this to engineering and design. There is back and forth and possibly a couple meetings to flesh things out. Design and Engineering will work at a fast stab to solve the problem. Design will schedule a meeting to go over high level design solution with engineering and product. Engineering will use this to design the architecture. Product will review the PRD, solution and create the epic which will include links to the PRD, architecture, and design.

div.div:
Planning
Monthly Leadership Roadmap Meeting - Anyone who has recently submitted an idea will come together and work to get space on the roadmap. We will also have inputs from engineering and trust functions for tech debt and security needs.
As need story mapping sessions: Once new Epics are thrown onto the roadmap, Product will plan for Story Mapping sessions. Design team will be charged with making detailed designs ahead of the story mapping sessions. Engineering will be charged with updating the ADR as needed before the story mapping sessions. Product will lead the story mapping sessions where the teams will
